overall: The AG found the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by approving three sets of minutes more than 30 days after their meetings and by omitting the individuals considered for annual appointments from the June 20 notice; it declined to review older minutes and ordered future compliance.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board failed to approve its March 26, March 28, and April 4 meeting minutes in a timely manner.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Board reviewed and approved them on June 20, more than 30 days after each meeting, it did not approve them in a timely manner.

allegations.summary: Complaint cited additional meeting minutes approved more than 30 days before the complaint was filed.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, we decline to review the additional meeting minutes cited in the complaint.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the June 20 notice failed to list the individuals considered for annual reappointment; the notice listed only '2018-2019 Annual Appointments'.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to list the individuals being considered for appointment on its June 20 meeting notice.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law (no further relief ordered because the Board lacked the benefit of the clarified guidance on notices).
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and we caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
